description:

Whether that experience is online or in-person, streaming video, theatrical, games, merchandise, events and more, it’s powered by the anime content we all love.

As part of our team, you’ll take ownership of tasks, delivering high-quality results on time, exceeding fans’ expectations. We foster collaboration, fearlessly exploring innovative solutions and challenging the status quo. Working with design, product, quality and data teams, you will solve complex challenges, optimize performance, and enhance user experience, directly contributing to the growth of the Crunchyroll fanbase.

Our day to day work includes integrations with payment providers, payments fraud detection and prevention, optimizations to reduce passive churn while maintaining PCI compliance. title: Product Specialist
description:
Fieldproxy is the AI-first field service platform for mid-market and enterprise operators. We replace legacy FSM tools like ServiceTitan, Simpro, ServiceM8 and IQ, plus spreadsheets, with software built around how each customer actually runs. That software is live in days, not months.

We’re hiring Solutions Architects to own that build, from the first discovery call to a team using it in the field.

What the role is

You’ll take a customer’s operation (dispatch, jobs, quotes, invoices, subcontractors, compliance, field apps) and turn it into a working Fieldproxy workspace. Often you’ll have it running before the sales call, so the prospect sees their own business in the demo.

You’ll build with AI in the loop. Most of the configuration is written with Claude Code and our internal skills. Your job is to know what good looks like, steer the build, check it against live data and ship it safely. You’re the person who knows whether the saved value comes back when the record is reopened, whether a status shows up on any list, and whether a write is properly gated.

What you’ll do

* **Run discovery.**
  Learn a customer’s workflow, the tools they use now and what they actually need. Write it up as a clear requirements doc and build plan.
* **Build tenants end to end:**
* PostgreSQL schemas and seed data
* web portals and mobile field apps (JSON-configured views, code widgets)
* customer-facing public forms: quote approvals, job trackers, sign-offs, payment links
* **Automate the operation**
  with Fieldproxy’s automation engine: SLA escalations, recurring work, inbound-email-to-job, PDF generation, reminders, webhooks.
* **Deploy AI**
  on customer workspaces:
* Command Center (ask and act on your data in plain English)
* SMS, email and voice agents
* AI extraction, summaries and scheduling
* MCP connections to Claude, ChatGPT and Grok
* **Integrate**
  with the systems customers already run: CRMs, accounting, helpdesks (Freshservice, Zoho), Shopify, Twilio, telematics, plus REST APIs and webhooks.
* **Migrate data**
  off legacy systems cleanly: imports, date and format traps, deduplication, reconciliation.
* **Validate before anything goes live.**
  Run our preflight and regression checks, test as real user roles, keep rollback versions, and never test against live customer data or send real emails or SMS from a build.
* **Present the solution**
  to owners, ops managers and finance leads. Explain what the system does in plain language, record walkthrough videos, and keep the customer hub up to date.
* **Support live customers.**
  Debug reported issues down to the root cause, fix them with a versioned change, and write up what happened.
* **Document what you build**
  so the next build is faster: reusable kits, patterns and known traps.

What we’re looking for

* **Strong SQL and PostgreSQL.**
  You read schemas fast, write correct joins and updates, and understand constraints, defaults, permissions and functions.
* **Comfortable with JSON and APIs.**
  Nested configs, REST and webhooks, auth headers. You can read an error and know where to look.
* **AI-native working style.**
  You already use Claude, Cursor or similar tools every day, and you check AI output instead of trusting it.
* **Systems thinking.**
  You see that a status written on the technician’s phone has to appear on the office list, and that a rule firing at 2 a.m. needs a timezone guard.
* **Customer sense.**
  You can sit with a fencing company or a facilities director, find the real problem, and push back on the wrong solution.
* **Clear communication**
  , written and spoken, with technical and non-technical people across the US, UK, Canada, Australia/NZ and India.
* **Ownership.**
  You ship, check your own work and close the loop with the customer without being chased.

Nice to have

* JavaScript, Python or HTML/CSS (code widgets and scripts)
* Experience with field service, construction, facilities or trades operations
* Experience with workflow automation (n8n, Zapier, Make) or LLM agents and tool calling
* Experience with Twilio, email deliverability or payments integrations

What we offer

* You’ll build real operations software for real companies every week, not slideware.
* You’ll work at the front of AI-first enterprise software: agents, MCP, AI-written configuration.
* You’ll work directly with the founding team and with customers, and have real say in what the product becomes.
* Competitive pay and fast growth as we scale.

title: Computational Linguist
description:
**About the role**

Moleculyst is building a reasoning checker that works directly in English. When an LLM draws conclusions from contracts, annexures or laws, our system checks every step for soundness and completeness against the source documents. We don’t formalize in Lean. Each step is an English sentence, read through a dictionary that can be corrected and checked against a small first-order logic core. We’re hiring a Computational Linguist to own the language side of this system.

**What you’ll work on**

* Parse English with the English Resource Grammar (ERG) and build our MRS-to-first-order-logic mapping
* Build DRS (Discourse Representation Theory) processing for multi-sentence text, covering anaphora, scope and reading pruning, kept domain-independent with no hand-written rules
* Design our controlled-English fragment, in the spirit of Attempto Controlled English. Many phrasings can map to one logical step, but one phrasing never maps to two.
* Build the WordNet-based sense dictionary, with LLM-driven sense selection and new entries, and people correcting wrong readings
* Turn pragmatics into a working spec: the questions an LLM must ask to resolve ambiguity, vagueness and missing context in queries, source documents and its own output, and when to ask a person
* Test the checker on real contracts and laws, using Z3 as a test oracle

**What we’re looking for**

* Strong formal semantics: first-order logic, DRT (Kamp & Reyle), MRS, quantifier scope, anaphora
* Grammar engineering experience, ideally with HPSG/ERG and DELPH-IN tools
* Lexical semantics and word sense disambiguation, with working knowledge of WordNet
* Grounding in pragmatics: presupposition, implicature, reference resolution
* Solid Python, and comfort working with LLMs, including locally hosted models
